newsitem.title: POLAND: EBRD, Polish bank agree on investment scheme.
newsitem.headline: EBRD, Polish bank agree on investment scheme.

text.p: A Polish bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development on Friday signed an agreement on an investment scheme aimed at helping financially troubled state-owned firms, the treasury ministry said.

The agreement is part of the government's programme called "Stabilisation Restructuring Privatisation," which provides for creating investment funds by the EBRD, Polish banks and the treasury which would take controlling stakes in the firms with a brief to sell them once they return to profit.
Under Friday's agreement, the EBRD and the Polish bank -- Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy, which belongs to the Pekao banking group -- would contribute equal capital to the fund.
The EBRD, which promised a total of $40 million for the programme, has signed similar agreements with Bank Depozytowo Kredytowy w Lublinie SA and Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA.

"The goal of the programe is to create a development chance for mid-size firms which have serious problems with financial liquidity but are capable of surviving in the market economy environment," the treasury ministry said in a statement.
Companies eligible to take part in the programme must have annual sales of at least 11.5 million zlotys ($3.7 million) and should not be involved in any other privatisation scheme.
